questions.stem: Two particles move with position vectors r_A(t) and r_B(t). What is the difference between their paths crossing and the particles meeting?
options: meeting needs the same point at the same time; crossing needs only the same point
crossing needs the same point at the same time; meeting needs only the same point
meeting needs equal velocities at some time; crossing needs equal positions
crossing needs parallel paths; meeting needs perpendicular paths
questions.explanation: Particles meet (collide) when r_A(t) = r_B(t) for one value of t. Their paths cross when some point lies on both paths, possibly reached at different times.

questions.stem: To decide whether two particles collide, the equation r_A(t) = r_B(t) is set up. What must be true for a collision?
options: one value of t satisfies every component equation
each component equation has a solution, with possibly different t values
the two position vectors are parallel for some t
the two velocity vectors are equal for some t
questions.explanation: A collision needs the particles at the same place at the same moment, so a single t must make the i, j and k components all equal. Different t values for different components mean no collision.

questions.stem: To test whether the paths of two particles cross, a student writes the paths as r_A(s) and r_B(u) with different parameters. Why?
options: the particles may reach a common point at different times
the two paths must always be described at different speeds
using one parameter would make the paths parallel
the paths can only cross if the parameters are unequal
questions.explanation: A crossing point only needs to lie on both paths, and each particle may pass it at its own time. Using the same t would test for a collision instead.

questions.stem: Particle A has r_A(t) = 2t i + (t + 1) j + (3 − t) k and particle B has r_B(t) = (t + 2) i + (3t − 3) j + (3 − t) k. When and where do they meet?
questions.explanation: The i components give 2t = t + 2, so t = 2. Then the j components are 3 and 3, and the k components are 1 and 1, so both are at (4, 3, 1) when t = 2.

questions.stem: Particle A has r_A(t) = (1 + 2t) i + (3 − t) j and particle B has r_B(t) = (4 − t) i + t j, for t ≥ 0. Which statement is true?
options: their paths do not cross, as the paths are parallel
the particles meet at (1, 3) when t = 0
their paths cross at (1, 3), but the particles do not meet
the particles meet at the point (3, 2) when t = 1
questions.explanation: For a meeting, the i components give t = 1 but the j components give t = 1.5, so they never meet. With separate parameters, 1 + 2s = 4 − u and 3 − s = u give s = 0, u = 3, so the paths cross at (1, 3) at different times.

questions.stem: Particle A moves on the path (t, 1 + t, 2t) and particle B on the path (1, s, 1 − s). How are the paths related?
options: they cross once, at the point (1, 2, 2)
they are parallel lines that never cross
they lie along the very same line
questions.explanation: Matching x gives t = 1, then y gives s = 2, but z gives 2 = −1, a contradiction, so the paths never cross. The directions (1, 1, 2) and (0, 1, −1) are not parallel, so the paths are skew.

questions.stem: Particle A has r_A(t) = 2t i + (t + 3) j and particle B has r_B(t) = (t + 4) i + (at − 1) j. For which value of a do the particles collide?
questions.explanation: The i components give 2t = t + 4, so t = 4. The j components must then agree: 4 + 3 = 4a − 1, so a = 2.

questions.stem: Two ships leave at the same time. Their positions in kilometres after t hours are P(t) = 3t i + 4t j and Q(t) = (18 − t) i + (4 + 2t) j. How long after P does Q reach the point where their paths cross?
questions.explanation: Solve 3s = 18 − u and 4s = 4 + 2u: s = 4 and u = 6, so the paths cross at (12, 16). P is there after 4 hours and Q after 6 hours, so Q arrives 2 hours later.

questions.stem: Particle A has r_A(t) = (1 + 2t) i + 3t j and particle B has r_B(t) = 4t i + (1 + 6t) j. Which statement is true?
options: the paths lie along the same line
the paths are parallel and never cross
the paths cross at exactly one point
questions.explanation: The direction vectors 2i + 3j and 4i + 6j are parallel. A passes through (1, 0) at t = 0, but B reaches x = 1 at t = 1/4 with y = 2.5, so the lines are distinct and never cross.

questions.stem: Particle A has r_A(t) = t i + 2t j and particle B has r_B(t) = (3 − t) i + (6 − 2t) j. Their paths both lie on y = 2x. Do they meet?
options: yes, at t = 1.5 at the point (1.5, 3)
no, because their paths are parallel
yes, at t = 3 at the point (3, 6)
no, because they move in opposite directions
questions.explanation: Equating components: t = 3 − t gives t = 1.5, and 2t = 6 − 2t also gives t = 1.5. So they meet at (1.5, 3). Moving towards each other along the same line is exactly how they collide.

questions.stem: Particles A and B have r_A(t) = t i + 2t j and r_B(t) = 3 i + (t + 1) j. What is the smallest distance between them?
questions.explanation: r_B − r_A = (3 − t) i + (1 − t) j, so the distance squared is (3 − t)² + (1 − t)² = 2t² − 8t + 10 = 2(t − 2)² + 2. The minimum is at t = 2, giving √2.

questions.stem: A system of linear equations that has no solution is called:
questions.explanation: A consistent system has at least one solution, and an inconsistent system has none. A homogeneous system has all constants zero, so it always has the solution x = y = z = 0.

questions.stem: Which values of x, y and z satisfy all three of x + y + z = 6, x − y + z = 2 and 2x + y − z = 1?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the second equation from the first gives 2y = 4, so y = 2. Then x + z = 4 and 2x − z = −1, which add to 3x = 3, so x = 1 and z = 3.

questions.stem: Solve x + 2y − z = 3, y + 3z = 7 and 2z = 4 by back substitution.
questions.explanation: z = 2, then y = 7 − 6 = 1, then x = 3 − 2y + z = 3 − 2 + 2 = 3. Writing x = 3 − 2 − 2 forgets that subtracting −z adds z.

questions.stem: In the system x + 2y + z = 4 and 3x + y − 2z = 1, the second equation is replaced by (second) − 3 × (first). What is the new equation?
questions.explanation: 3x − 3x = 0, y − 6y = −5y, −2z − 3z = −5z and 1 − 12 = −11. Subtracting 3z from −2z, rather than adding, is a common slip.

questions.stem: Adults pay $20, children $10 and concessions $15. Ticket sales were 100 tickets for $1650, with twice as many child tickets as concession tickets. How many adult tickets were sold?
What does a single linear equation in x, y and z represent geometrically?
questions.explanation: An equation ax + by + cz = d describes a plane with normal vector (a, b, c). A line in three dimensions needs two equations, or a vector equation.

questions.stem: A system of three linear equations in x, y and z has a unique solution. What does this mean geometrically?
options: two of the three planes coincide
the three planes meet at a single point
the three planes meet in a common line
questions.explanation: Each equation is a plane, and a unique solution is a single point lying on all three. A common line would give infinitely many solutions.

questions.stem: During elimination on a system of three equations, one equation becomes 0x + 0y + 0z = 5. What does this show?
options: the system has the solution x = y = z = 0
the system has exactly one solution
the system has infinitely many solutions
questions.explanation: No values of x, y and z make 0 equal 5, so the system is inconsistent. A row reducing to 0 = 0 would instead allow infinitely many solutions.

questions.stem: During elimination, one equation of a three-variable system becomes 0 = 0, and the other two are consistent and not multiples of each other. How many solutions are there?
options: exactly two, one for each equation
questions.explanation: The 0 = 0 row gives no information, leaving two independent equations in three unknowns. One variable is free, so the solutions form a line.

questions.stem: Three planes, no two of which are parallel, have no point in common. How are they arranged?
options: two of the planes coincide and the third crosses them
each pair meets in a line, and the three lines are parallel
all three meet in a single common line
all three meet at a single common point
questions.explanation: With no parallel planes, each pair intersects in a line. No common point means these three lines never meet, so they are parallel, forming a triangular prism shape.

questions.stem: Three distinct planes have infinitely many points in common. How are they arranged?
options: they all pass through one common line
they are all parallel to each other
they meet at exactly one point
questions.explanation: Distinct planes cannot share more than a line, so infinitely many common points means a common line, like the pages of a book along the spine.

questions.stem: A system contains 2x − y + 3z = 4 and 4x − 2y + 6z = 5. What can be said about the system?
options: it has a unique solution, because the coefficients are different
it has no solution, because the planes are perpendicular
it has no solution, because these planes are parallel and distinct
it has infinitely many solutions, because the planes coincide
questions.explanation: The second equation has the same left side as twice the first, but 5 ≠ 8, so the planes are parallel and do not coincide. No point lies on both, whatever the other equations are.

questions.stem: Consider just the two equations x + y − z = 1 and 2x − y + z = 5. What is their solution set?
options: x = 2, y = t + 1, z = t for any real t
x = 2, y = t − 1, z = t for any real t
questions.explanation: Adding gives 3x = 6, so x = 2, and then y − z = −1. Letting z = t gives y = t − 1, a line of solutions; (2, −1, 0) is just one point on it.

questions.stem: For which value of k does the system x + y + z = 2, x + 2y + 3z = 5, 2x + 3y + kz = 8 have no solution?
questions.explanation: Eliminating x gives y + 2z = 3 and y + (k − 2)z = 4, so (k − 4)z = 1. When k = 4 this reads 0 = 1, so there is no solution; any other k gives a unique solution.

questions.stem: For which value of c does the system x + y + z = 2, x + 2y + 3z = 5, 2x + 3y + 4z = c have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation: Eliminating x gives y + 2z = 3 and y + 2z = c − 4. These agree only when c − 4 = 3, so c = 7; any other c makes the system inconsistent.

questions.stem: With c = 7, the system x + y + z = 2, x + 2y + 3z = 5, 2x + 3y + 4z = 7 has infinitely many solutions. Which is a general solution?
questions.explanation: From y + 2z = 3, with z = t, y = 3 − 2t. Then x = 2 − y − z = 2 − 3 + 2t − t = t − 1. Substituting each other option into x + y + z = 2 fails.
